parts.text: A student investigates the cooling of water. Fig. 2.1 shows the set-up. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The thermometer in Fig. 2.2 shows the room temperature θ R at the beginning of the experiment. Record θ R . Fig. 2.2 θ R = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student pours 200 cm 3 of hot water into a beaker. He places a lid on the beaker. He places the thermometer in the hot water in the beaker. He records, in Table 2.1, the temperature θ of the hot water at time t = 0. He immediately starts a stop-watch. He continues recording the temperature in Table 2.1 at 30 s intervals until he has seven sets of readings.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Complete the column headings in Table 2.1. [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Write the times in the first column of Table 2.1. Table 2.1 t / θ / 92 87 83 80 78 76 75 [1]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Calculate the decrease in temperature Δθ between t = 0 and t = 180 s. Δθ = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the average rate of cooling R of the water using the equation R = Δθ Δ t , where Δ t = 180 s. Include the unit. R = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
any two from:

remove lid

thinner lid

paint the beaker black

stir the water

change beaker to container that is a better conductor / named metal

increase surface (area of water / beaker)

use a wider beaker

blow air over water surface / use a fan

use a smaller volume of water

ms.label: 2(e)
ms.text:
statement: view thermometer / scale / reading at right angles / eye level
explanation: to avoid parallax error
OR
statement: stir (before taking reading)
explanation: to distribute water evenly / to ensure that all the water is at the same temperature
OR
statement: ensure thermometer does not touch the side / base of beaker
explanation: temperature different to that of the bulk of the liquid
OR
statement: wait until the thermometer (reading) stops rising at the start
explanation: so that the maximum temperature of the liquid is recorded

ms.label: 2(f)
ms.text: negligible / very small volume / amount of water between the bottom and the top of the meniscus
